extracted.intended_audience: patent litigators and practitioners drafting bills/complaints in equity for patent infringement (and law students studying patent pleading rules)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and legal standards for drafting bills in equity (complaints) in patent-infringement litigation, including required averments, joinder rules, and the form of equitable relief requested. Focuses on what must be alleged and how causes/parties may be joined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonjoinder of Defendants
rubrics_metrics.description: The nonjoinder of defendants is no ground of defence unless the account of profits is inseparable, or for some other reason the presence of the omitted parties is indispensable to a decree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The absence of proper defendants must be taken advantage of by demurrer, plea, or answer; the objection must set forth the connection of such persons with the cause of action and allege that they are within the territorial jurisdiction of the court. If sustained, the court may order the persons to appear and be made parties; if the order cannot be enforced the court will stay proceedings or dismiss the bill. An amendment changing the capacity in which defendants have been sued that in effect creates a new defendant cannot be allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bill must disclose substantial groundwork / aver every material fact
rubrics_metrics.description: A bill in equity in actions for infringement must disclose the substantial groundwork of the case and contain averments covering every material fact; the court has no authority to consider what is proved and not alleged, or what is alleged and not supported by the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the bill fails to allege the substantial groundwork, no decree can be rendered; the bill should not rely on evidence to supply omissions in the pleadings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material facts to be alleged (five fundamental questions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The material facts in equity (as at law) relate to five questions: (1) the performance by the alleged inventor of an inventive act resulting in the alleged invention; (2) the existence and validity of a patent protecting this invention; (3) the title of the plaintiff to that patent; (4) the infringement of that patent by the defendant; and (5) the damage sustained by the plaintiff, and the benefits accruing to the defendant from the infringing acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The bill should contain averments addressing each of these five matters; these are the core matters the court must be apprised of in the pleadings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description and profert of the patent / sufficiency of patent averment
rubrics_metrics.description: The averment of the patent may describe it by date and title with a profert; the patent may be annexed or profert made or the language of the specification may be employed, or the pleader may give a full and accurate description in his own words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent is not properly described or proferted, the bill may be demurrable. Referring to and making profert of the patent or employing the specification's language generally suffices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invention description must apprise court (and bar on public-use/onsale)
rubrics_metrics.description: A bill must describe the invention, not merely by date and number of the patent, but so fully as to apprise the court of its nature and characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The bill must allege that the invention was not in public use or on sale for more than two years before the application. History of the art and prior patents/litigation may properly be averred where relevant to the controversy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Averment of title (what to state and when)
rubrics_metrics.description: The averment of title may allege the plaintiff's interest in the patent without reciting the chain of title or declaring recording of conveyances, but it must define the right in which he sues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the plaintiff relies on a former verdict and judgment to show his titles or right to equitable relief, the bill must aver that judgment. An assignment of exclusive rights may require additional averments (e.g., to show defendants are not operating under a licensee).

rubrics_metrics.name: Averment of infringement: general allegations permitted but must be positive and certain
rubrics_metrics.description: The averment of infringement need not describe the particular acts performed by the defendant nor point out portions appropriated; a general allegation that the defendant has infringed is deemed sufficient to put him upon his answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nevertheless the allegation must be positive and certain and disclose such circumstances of time, place, and method as show upon the face of the averment that the rights have been invaded. Allegations must not be merely hypothetical or argumentative. An allegation phrased disjunctively (e.g., 'making or selling') is improper, though if the bill alleges both making and selling it is sustained by evidence of either. Phrases like 'has built and is now using' have been held insufficient to aver present use of what was built. Allegations that the defendant is making and using devices 'in some parts' substantially the same may be sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allegations concerning conveyances, licenses, and multiple defendants
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the plaintiff has conveyed assignable interests outstanding when infringement was committed, the averment of infringement must deny that the defendant used the invention under such conveyance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a plaintiff has sold an exclusive right for a term, the bill must set out that the defendant is not operating under the licensee. Where there is more than one defendant, the relation among them must be sufficiently delineated to indicate that all participate in the infringing acts. When officers of a corporation are made parties, their status as officers should be averred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Averment of damages and profits
rubrics_metrics.description: The averment of damages may be in general terms; the averment of profits must set forth such facts as to the mode in which the defendant has practised the invention, and the benefits he has thence derived, as will show there have been pecuniary gains or savings for which the plaintiff is entitled to an account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the advantage to the defendant can only be estimated as a whole or cannot be shown to result in profits (from the nature of the invention or the method of infringement), an account in equity may be improper and the bill may be dismissed. Profits may be alleged as general or special; actual profits appearing on accounting will be covered by the averment if properly pled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of allegations: no reliance on evidence to supply pleadings
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill must aver every material fact, for the court cannot consider what is proved and not alleged, or what is alleged and not supported by evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not omit essential averments expecting to supply them at trial; pleadings must present the substantial groundwork of the case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prayers for equitable relief — general requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill must close with a prayer for the desired relief; the relief sought must be, in part at least, of such a character as equity alone can grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the bill prays for damages only, and in most cases where it prays for profits only, it presents no ground for equitable interference. To invoke equity the bill should unite a prayer for injunction, discovery, or some other remedy not obtainable at law, unless other portions of the bill make it apparent that equity alone affords adequate redress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific averments required for injunctions
rubrics_metrics.description: When an injunction is requested, the bill must state facts which render it necessary and must show the plaintiff's title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The bill must state that the defendant threatens to commit or refuses to desist from an infringement. If the injunction is to precede trial, the bill should aver a prior judgment sustaining the plaintiff's right, or long continued public acquiescence in the exercise of the plaintiff's exclusive privilege, or other circumstances justifying preliminary equitable relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific averments required for discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: When the bill prays for a discovery the plaintiff must point out the facts concerning which disclosure is required and allege the inability to establish them by any evidence at his command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prayer for discovery must indicate the precise points for disclosure and the absence of other evidence; general requests without specified needs are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joinder of causes based on several patents (when allowed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where several patents belonging to the plaintiff are violated by the same infringement on the part of the defendant, these different causes of action may be united and relief for the entire injury may be afforded in a single suit; a bill is not multifarious merely because it counts upon numerous patents or alleges various infringing acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts encourage single suits to avoid multiplicity of actions, provided the matters are sufficiently connected and the joinder does not unfairly embarrass the defendant's defence. Suits on an original invention and on an improvement are not divisible if both patents belong to the same owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multifariousness / when joinder is improper
rubrics_metrics.description: A bill is multifarious when it joins matters perfectly distinct, or demands remedies of an independent character against separate defendants; a defendant cannot be compelled to unite wholly different defences in his answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No universal test exists; the court exercises sound discretion. If the multiplicity of claims will embarrass the defendant, confuse proofs, protract the controversy, or impose unnecessary costs, the bill may be treated as defective and required to be simplified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that inventions be capable of conjoint use for joinder
rubrics_metrics.description: If several patents are to be included in one suit, their subjects-matter must be correlative and capable of conjoint use in the infringing process or device; the bill must allege, and the evidence must prove, the joint employment of the several inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the inventions are incapable of united use or are applied to separate uses by the defendant, the infringements are distinct and a bill counting on more than one of them is multifarious. In suits on multiple patents, failure to aver that infringing machines contain all the improvements embraced in the several patents may render the bill multifarious on demurrer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joinder limits when devices are used separately
rubrics_metrics.description: One bill cannot embrace infringements of two wholly separate patents for machines/devices unless the devices are used conjointly; if one device is used in one machine and another in another, joinder is improper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where each invention is capable of separate use and trial as to validity and infringement would produce distinct issues, the bill may be multifarious. Alleging five patents infringed by one machine can still be multifarious if each invention is separately usable and would require separate trials on validity and infringement.
